title: Is The legendary Howling Ray’s in LA worth the hype?
Is this LA’s most iconic sandwich 🇺🇸
Reviewing LA smash burgers with Pete and Bas
Reviewing Korean Salt bread in LA
Iran V New Zealand at the World Cup ⚽️
Trying late night tacos in LA 🌮
LA’s best Mexican seafood 🍤
Trying Cambodian food for the first time at Barang in borough ￼ market

restaurants.name: Barang
restaurants.notes: Cambodian cuisine. Gerry gave 9.5/10, Paul gave 9.4/10. They were extremely impressed with multiple dishes including pork mince on toast with pickled mussels (described as 'one of the dishes of the year'), the curries, and deep fried seabream. They called it 'one of the best meals we had this year' and 'stunning'.

title: London’s newest chicken Caesar wrap any good?

restaurants.name: Wingman's
restaurants.notes: Chicken Caesar wrap reviewed favorably. They praise the crispy chicken skin, creamy spicy sauce, grated Parmesan, and the perfect ratio of chicken to salad. They note it's a good quick lunch option in Soho without long wait times and you can book online.

restaurants.name: Cafe de Frango
restaurants.notes: Described as the best Portuguese restaurant in London. Reviewers praised the fish (sea bass described as 'some of the best fish I've ever had'), the piri piri chicken ('some of the best chicken I've ever had, perfectly juicy'), and various Portuguese dishes like bacalhau and pork croquettes. Venue was noted as absolutely stunning.

title: Does a full Scottish breakfast beat a full English ? 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿

restaurants.name: Old Hag
restaurants.notes: They reviewed a full Scottish breakfast here. Gerry gave it 7.9/10, Paul gave it 7.7/10. Both acknowledged it was a solid breakfast with abundant portions, though Gerry felt the egg could have been more runny and Paul preferred the Full English overall. Priced at £17.50.

title: Is Brighton new Philly cheesesteak hole steak hole in the wall any good?
Is this London’s best pastel de nata? 🇵🇹

restaurants.name: The Santa Nata
restaurants.notes: Portuguese tart specialist. Gerry praised the gooey warm custard and crispy caramelized shell, though Paul found it too sweet and gloopy, rating it 6.4. They only sell one item - pastel de nata.

title: When 2 Michelin chef’s join forces at Galvin La Chapelle 🤌🏽

restaurants.name: Galvin La Chapelle
restaurants.notes: Michelin star restaurant with guest chef Tom Brown. Beautifully executed meal featuring duck liver parfait, lobster, sea green, crab custard, lamb trio, and coconut parfait. Described as one of the best meals they've had.

title: Is this the best sandwich in Brighton ?
Reviewing bougi fish and chips at one of London’s oldest oyster bars 🐠

restaurants.name: Bentley's
restaurants.notes: One of London's oldest oyster bars and bougie fish and chip places, serving oysters for 150 years. Gerry and Paul praised the fish and chips as some of the best they've ever had, with perfectly flaky fish, crispy batter, excellent curry sauce, and superb chips.

title: We reviewed vegan fish and chips, in the sea 🍃
£5 for loaded Doritos worth it?

restaurants.name: Spud Bros Express
restaurants.notes: Gerry gave it 7.2/10, Paul gave it 6.8/10. They reviewed loaded Doritos nachos for £5. Gerry found it gimmicky but tasty and worth it occasionally; Paul thought it was fun and not expensive but somewhat trashy, with both appreciating the generous toppings and nice chili/cream sauce.

title: Is Brighton’s newest pizza spot worthy of the hype? 🍕
Is this London’s best burger? 🍔

restaurants.name: Lagom
restaurants.notes: Exceptional burger with high-end beef, soft bun, and dill vinegar. Despite initial visual disappointment, the taste was outstanding - buttery, juicy meat with distinctive vinegar notes.

title: Is Goldies off Carnaby street worthy of the hype?

restaurants.name: Goldie's
restaurants.notes: Elevated hot dogs and burgers with excellent ribs that Paul rated 9.8/10 as his favorite dish. Both reviewers praised the quality and execution, with creative twists on classic comfort food.

title: Is the new m&s custard cream cookie any good? 🍪

restaurants.name: M&S
restaurants.notes: Reviewed their new custard cream cookie which tasted like a gooey cookie with lovely custard cream flavors. Paul gave it an 8 out of 10, praising it as a 'perfect budget cookie' for £2.10 that was 'banging' and 'really nice'. Also tried the pistachio variant which had good texture but okay flavor.

title: Brighton’s oldest ice cream parlour 🍦

restaurants.name: Morrocans
restaurants.notes: Famous ice cream parlour established in 1969. They make their ice cream in-house in the basement. Both presenters praised the ice cream flavours including Biscoff, peanut and pretzel, and millionaire's shortbread with pink grapefruit as delicious and refreshing.

title: Is the magnolia bakery in London worth the 30 mins queue? 🍌

restaurants.name: The Magnolia Bakery
restaurants.notes: Their banana pudding is exceptional and creamy with the right blend of cakey bits and banana lumps. Both presenters felt this London version was even better than the New York original, and they would queue for it again.

title: Is the viral Czer wrap worth the hour queue?

restaurants.name: Czer
restaurants.notes: Viral Caesar chicken salad wrap. Fresh and crunchy but not worth the hour-long queue. One presenter scored 7.8, the other scored 6.4. Good texture with crisps and jalapenos, but chicken content is low.

title: Does London have decent banana pudding? 🍌

restaurants.name: Benji's
restaurants.notes: Reviewed their banana pudding. Gerry gave it 7.8/10, praising it as naturally banana-y and creamy, though noting it lacks chunks of banana. Paul gave it 6.6/10, finding it less authentic tasting and less satisfying than Magnolia Bakery in New York.

title: Best ice cream in London?

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Ice cream shop with excellent flavors including salted caramel, Oreo cheesecake, raspberry cheesecake, and salted caramel cookie dough. Paul rated it 8/10 and Gerry gave it 8.3/10. Praised for high-quality, clean ice cream made with love and not trying to be a traditional Italian gelateria.

title: Is this London’s best Sunday roast?

restaurants.name: Black Horse Grill
restaurants.notes: Excellent Sunday roast with outstanding Yorkshire puddings (9.5/10 for flavor), juicy and perfectly charred chicken and pork with exceptional crackling. Beautifully executed sides including crunchy sprouts, good roast potatoes, charred cauliflower cheese, and sweet carrots. Exceptional gravy. Highly recommended by the reviewers.

title: Supper club in an old church 😇

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: A supper club in an old church in Mayfair. They enjoyed multiple dishes including chili sweet potato tostada, chili lamb chops, paneer tikka, garlic bread, jalapeño hummus, and garlic pepper prawns. The presenters praised the multicultural menu, flavorful dishes, and overall experience as 'an absolute whirlwind' with 'good food, good company, good cooking.'

title: Is this viral London bakery worthy of the hype?

restaurants.name: Pandera
restaurants.notes: Filipino bakery. The ube donut was excellent (8.2), miso cinnamon roll was decent but a bit dry (7.4), and chicken Caesar wrap/sausage roll were just okay (7.3). Overall rating 7.8 - good items but not entirely worthy of the hype.

restaurants.name: Ginger Pig
restaurants.notes: Mentioned as having 'ruined sausage rolls' for everyone else in the industry with their slam dunk product, making other sausage rolls seem mediocre by comparison.

title: Is the Guinness pie at the Guinness brewery any good? 🥧

restaurants.name: Guinness Factory
restaurants.notes: Reviewed the beef and Guinness pie (£14 with mash). Gerry gave it 8.4/10, praising the tasty gravy, rich beef, and quality despite the price. Paul gave it 7.9/10, finding it good but slightly bland on the Guinness flavour and small in portion size.

title: Does Bancone really do the best pasta in a London? 🍝

restaurants.name: Bancone
restaurants.notes: Reviewers praised the pasta quality, particularly highlighting the carbonara as one of the best they've eaten. They were impressed by the visible pasta preparation, fresh al dente pasta, and creative dishes like the creamy maltagliati with rare breed beef and fried artichoke.

title: Is the Claridge’s club sandwich worth it? 🥪

restaurants.name: Claridge's
restaurants.notes: Their £40 club sandwich was mediocre and poorly executed. Gerry and Paul found it underwhelming compared to the Savoy, with bland flavors, cheap-tasting bread, and not worth the price. The chips were decent but the overall experience was lackluster.

title: Trying Pho for the first time 🍜

restaurants.name: Viet Rest
restaurants.notes: Reviewed pho for the first time in Little Hanoi, Deptford. Gerry gave it 7 out of 10, praising the rare beef pho as having good silky saltiness and clean, healthy flavours with nice herbs and lemongrass. Paul gave it 7.6, calling it one of the cleanest and most refreshing things he'd eaten, though felt it didn't give the taste buds a 'roller coaster' experience.

title: Ginger Pig sausages are life 🐽

restaurants.name: Ginger Pig
restaurants.notes: Reviewed their full range of sausages including smoked jalapeno, pork and pepper, lamb merguez, traditional, and Scotch bonnet. Presenters praised the quality of the meat and described them as 'the best in the game', with particular favorites being the Scotch bonnet and jalapeno sausages.

title: Lewisham’s Italian deli 🇮🇹

restaurants.name: Antonio's
restaurants.notes: Italian deli with a long history in the community. Formerly called Gennaro's. Known for quality ingredients and classic Italian sandwiches at good value. They tried a bresaola sandwich with Parmesan, lettuce and tomatoes, which they found delicious with beautifully crunchy bread.

title: We answer your questions!

restaurants.name: Carmela's
restaurants.notes: Gerry and Paul's own pizzeria where they were filming. They praised the tomato pie as one of the best pizzas they've ever had.

restaurants.name: Crazy Pizza
restaurants.notes: They tried the smoked salmon and caviar pizza (about £68) and found it tasteless and absolutely wrong in every way. Cited as their biggest rip-off.

restaurants.name: Ethiopian restaurant
restaurants.notes: Paul described it as absolutely beautiful, nutritious, healthy, and tasty. Cited as a biggest surprise delight.

restaurants.name: Brick Lane food market vendor
restaurants.notes: Paul couldn't remember the specific vendor name but praised the food at the upmarket food market on Brick Lane.

restaurants.name: Kude's
restaurants.notes: Gerry raved about their cookies, calling them outrageous and taking cookies to the absolute next level. He's been thinking about them in his dreams.

restaurants.name: Binchotan
restaurants.notes: Paul said the first Binchotan spice pizza he had there was good. Listed as one of the best pizzas he's ever had.

restaurants.name: Brooklyn DOP
restaurants.notes: Paul listed this as one of the best pizzas he's had and said they really enjoyed it, though he didn't fully remember it when Gerry mentioned it.

title: VIP treatment at the world famous Connaught bar 🍸

restaurants.name: Connaught
restaurants.notes: Reviewed their cocktails including their famous martini, old fashioned, Long Island Iced Tea, and various other cocktails. Both presenters praised the drinks as exquisite, sophisticated, and delicious throughout their visit.

title: Is this London’s coolest Greek restaurant ? 🇬🇷

restaurants.name: The Apollo
restaurants.notes: Greek restaurant praised for high-quality dishes including perfectly buttered bread, creamy spicy feta, well-prepared calamari, yellowtail tuna, lamb belly, lamb chops, and ribeye steak. Gerry gave 9.2, Paul gave 9.0.

title: We review KFC’s hottest burger ever

restaurants.name: KFC
restaurants.notes: Reviewed their Sriracha Firecracker burger which they found underwhelming, dry, not actually hot or tasty despite claims of being their hottest burger yet. Priced at £6.99.

title: Reviewing the Michelin starred pud in South London

restaurants.name: Kerfield Arms
restaurants.notes: Michelin-starred pub offering an exceptional £15 lunch deal with main and drink. Excellent pork with buttery glaze, creamy parsley sauce, and fluffy bread with crispy exterior. Unpretentious neighborhood boozer with exceptional service.

restaurants.name: Theo's
restaurants.notes: Mentioned as part of Camberwell's emerging food scene, but not reviewed in this video.

restaurants.name: Camberwell Arms
restaurants.notes: Mentioned as part of Camberwell's emerging food scene, but not reviewed in this video.

restaurants.name: Brindisa
restaurants.notes: Mentioned as part of Camberwell's emerging food scene, but not reviewed in this video.

title: Is this London’s best burger? 🍔

restaurants.name: Meatstock at the Commercial Tavern
restaurants.notes: Gerry and Paul reviewed Meatstock's burgers at their new residency. Gerry gave the classic burger 9.3/10, praising it as better than Popl in Copenhagen, with buttery Essex farm meat and excellent quality. Paul gave the Blue Magic burger 9.4/10, highlighting the stilton, caramelized onions, and perfect seasoning.

title: Reviewing scotch eggs in Borough Market 👀

restaurants.name: Ginger Pig
restaurants.notes: They tried the Ginger Pig's Scotch egg (£5.50). The presenters praised the quality of the meat and seasoning, though they felt it would have been better served hot rather than cold. Paul gave it 7.5/10 and Gerry gave it 7.4/10. They also recommended their sausage rolls.

title: Reviewing the viral Guinness cake for st Patrick’s day ☘️

restaurants.name: Seven Dials Market
restaurants.notes: They reviewed the viral Guinness pudding which they praised highly - describing it as gooey, tasty with tons of Guinness flavour, not too sweet, with nice texture and chocolate speckles. They also tried a chocolate caramel dessert which was good but not as good as the Guinness pudding.

title: Bling Tasting Irish stouts. Could you tell which one is Guiness? 🤔

restaurants.name: The Colonel Faucett
restaurants.notes: They visited for a blind stout tasting and Irish food. The food impressed them more than expected with outstanding dishes like the white pudding scotch egg (described as 'one of the better ones in London'), Cashel Blue croquettes, Dublin Bay prawns with soda bread, and beef and Guinness stew (rated 8.7-10 out of 10). Paul gave the stew a 10/10, praising it as 'profoundly Irish' with deep, meaty, rich flavors.

title: North London’s best bakery?

restaurants.name: Jolene
restaurants.notes: They enjoyed the bakery items, particularly praising the flavours as delicious and well-balanced. The rhubarb pastry had great flavours but they felt the pastry could be crunchier. They also tried a savoury option with jalapenos that had good crunch and heat.

title: Would you pay £11 for a cheese toastie?

restaurants.name: Poosie's Deli
restaurants.notes: Reviewed their cheese toasty (£11, triple cheese with kimchi on Dusty Knuckle bread) and sausage roll (£5). The cheese toasty was highly praised as one of the better they've had - very gooey with a nice crunch to the bread and flavourful kimchi.

title: Are the viral m&s doughnuts any good?

restaurants.name: Bread Ahead
restaurants.notes: Mentioned as having excellent donuts that would 'blow your mind' in comparison to M&S donuts, implying their donuts are of much higher quality.

title: South London full English brekkie

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Solid full English breakfast with good sausage, bacon, eggs, tomato, beans, and fried slice. Gerry gave it 7.1, Paul gave it 10.2. The boss has been running the place for 36 years; feels homely and is full of local South Londoners.

title: The £25 Pie Burger 🍔🥧

restaurants.name: Roe
restaurants.notes: Michelin-starred restaurant with creative pie-themed dishes including a £25 cheeseburger pie. Presenters praised the quality of the meats, creative concepts, and overall execution, though they had mixed views on the bread. Both rated it highly (8.4 and 8.3) and confirmed the pie burger was worth trying for Pie Week.

title: Is this London’s best banh mi? #food

restaurants.name: Clifton Street Market
restaurants.notes: Reviewed multiple banh mi sandwiches at this market vendor. The pork banh mi was noted as incredibly juicy and delicious with roasted, caramelized meat, though they wanted crispier bread. The ox heart banh mi (£12) scored 8.6 for its unusual ingredients and perfect juiciness, though some found the meat chewy.

title: It’s pie week so we went and ate £25 pie & mash Manze’s X Wolseley collab #pietime

restaurants.name: Manze's
restaurants.notes: They reviewed a £25 pie and mash collaboration with The Wolseley for National Pie Week. Both presenters loved it, calling it "probably the best pie I've ever eaten" with deeply creamy mash, rich buttery gravy, and excellent pastry.

title: Reviewing the South London Palestinian bakery #food #londoners

restaurants.name: Bun Head
restaurants.notes: Palestinian bakery with British baking fusion. Reviewers were extremely impressed with the cinnamon bun (juicy, soft, with unfamiliar but pleasant Palestinian flavors) and the chocolate sourdough pastry (not too sweet, excellent chocolate flavor with good aftertaste). Gerry gave it 9.3/10, noting that if slightly warmer could be closer to 10.

title: Why is Pizza Hut dying?

restaurants.name: Pizza Hut
restaurants.notes: Revisited their childhood Pizza Hut location. Found the pizza to be weak, anemic, pale, and lacking in flavor - described as barely edible, overly greasy, and a disappointing shadow of their nostalgic memories. The salad bar was noted as more extensive than the pizza selection, and the ice cream was very sandy and tasted like nothing.

title: 5p chicken shawarma in London 🤯

restaurants.name: Ali and Shawarma Hut
restaurants.notes: 5p chicken shawarma special (normally £4.99). Fresh, juicy, tender meat with charred bits and generous portions. Owner runs a charitable food bank, feeding homeless and families with no conditions. Amazing value and community work.

title: Trying a Spice bag for the first time 🇮🇪

restaurants.name: Molly Malone's
restaurants.notes: Tried their spice bag (chicken for £14) for the first time. Described it as 'filthy', 'delicious', 'dodgy', 'salty', 'spicy' - fusion of Chinese and Irish chippy food that they loved.

restaurants.name: O'Donoghues
restaurants.notes: Irish singing pub visited for the launch of Paul's fifth book on historic pub crawls. Paul stated he absolutely loves this place.

title: At £65 is this the cheapest Michelin starred tasting menu?

restaurants.name: Behind
restaurants.notes: Michelin-starred restaurant offering an intimate tasting menu at £65. Described as excellent value for a Michelin-starred experience with innovative dishes including prawn consommé, hand-dived scallops, and various seafood preparations. Reviewers found it to be the best value lunchtime set deal available.

title: £22 for two pastries 🤯

restaurants.name: Coper
restaurants.notes: Gluten-free French bakery. Gerry and Paul found the pastries extremely disappointing and dry, with dull vanilla flavor. Two pastries cost £22 total (£18.90 and £21.60). They gave scores of 2.2, 2.1, and 2.4 out of 10.

title: Reviewing Turkish Gozleme

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Spicy lamb gozleme with fresh preparation. Presenters found the bread leathery and not juicy, though tasty. They preferred other options like tantuni for the same price. Would benefit from dipping sauce.

restaurants.name: Gozleme House
restaurants.notes: Mentioned as being a few doors down. Presenters noted they didn't offer dipping sauce, which was a negative point.

title: Reviewing Kate Moss brothers Banh Mi outfit 🇻🇳

restaurants.name: Viet Van
restaurants.location: East Dulwich, North Cross Road Market
restaurants.notes: Half and half banh mi (chicken and pork) with juicy meat, great sauces, and bread that holds up well. Described as a British twist on banh mi, £11.

title: Did you know there is a restaurant in East London in a denim factory?

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Restaurant in a denim factory serving creative dishes like pumpkin with pomegranate dressing, oxtail with sweet potato, pasta with creamy fillings, Vietnamese spiced pork, and sticky toffee dessert. Presenters praised the food quality, textures, flavors, and pleasant environment.

title: Eating at London’s only Austrian restaurant 🇦🇹

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: London's only Austrian restaurant. Reviewers praised the schnitzel, kipferl soup, Austrian meatballs, escalope, and Kaiserschmarrn pancake. They recommend the place with enthusiasm and vigor.

title: Londons cheapest eats! Meals for £5 or less

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: £5 fry up with sausage, eggs, beans, mushrooms and chips. Described as 'Master Chef of deals' and 'unbeatable for £5 in 2026'.

restaurants.name: Bosworth Collab
restaurants.notes: £3.50 chicken shawarma wrap located at the back of a Syrian grocery store. 'Sits at the top of the league. Amazing' with flaky bread, tender charred meat, and fresh salad.

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Turkish tantuni restaurant with one item on menu - double wrap with chopped lamb, seasoning, herbs, and lemon zest for 50p. 'Flavor in abundance' with 'luscious' meat and zingy spice.

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: 100-year-old pie and mash shop (opened 1926) serving two pies and mash for £4.40. Described as 'comforting food', 'like a hug from your nan', with thick gravy and gluey mash.

title: Reviewing London’s first Welsh bakery/cafe 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿

restaurants.name: Bara
restaurants.notes: London's first Welsh bakery/café that opened on a soft launch. They make all their own bread in-house. Bite Twice tried their birth cake (Welsh fruit loaf), miso cookie, and another cookie - all highly praised for being moist, well-baked, and having excellent texture and flavour.

title: Is this the UK’s best burger? 🍔

restaurants.name: Smiths Burger
restaurants.notes: Award-winning burger restaurant. Reviewers gave individual burgers ratings of 8.1, 9, 8.5, and 8.9 out of 10, describing them as high quality with excellent flavors including miso mayonnaise, black garlic, Marmite, and blue cheese elements.

title: Is the winner of the bakers dozen award really the best bakery in the UK?

restaurants.name: August Bakery
restaurants.notes: Won the Baker's Dozen award. Outstanding pastries including rhubarb, cardamom bun, and serrano ham pastry. Excellent coffee with silky, creamy foam. Gerry and Paul considered it one of the best bakeries in London and were impressed it opened just last year and already tops rankings.

title: London’s best kebab?

restaurants.name: Hassos
restaurants.notes: Outstanding quality kebab meat - described as some of the best they've had - but pricey at £15.99 for two breads. Lacks sauce and they were eating on the street rather than inside, which affected the experience. Highly recommended to eat in-house.

title: Is Romesh Ranganathan’s bakery actually any good?

restaurants.name: Offley's Bakery
restaurants.notes: Tried their crème brûlée croissant (£3.80), which they praised as a masterclass in pastry filling with proper flavour balance, crunchy textures, and creamy filling. They highlighted it as a reason to visit Croydon and called it Offley's winner from their previous visits.

title: Trying Alcohol free beer that gives you a buzz 🍺

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Gerry and Paul had pizza here while testing alcohol-free beer. They praised it as "one of the best pizzas in London" with buttery, juicy, crunchy sausage and crispy, silky smooth crust.

title: London’s best bakery?

restaurants.name: Fred Bakery
restaurants.notes: Reviewers tried multiple pastries including a chocolate product (£5.50) which they found divine, creamy, and elegant, and a pistachio and berry jam puff pastry (£7) which was very tasty though one reviewer wouldn't pay £7 again. Both gave individual scores of 8.2 and 8.3 out of 10.

title: Is the 3 Michelin star bakery worthy of the hype?

restaurants.name: Sue
restaurants.notes: Japanese bakery with poor queue management and staff service. Items tasted underwhelming - the purple yam bun tasted like mashed potato in a bun, and the kumquat and lemon cheesecake (£6.50) was overly sweet, acidic, with a weird texture that fell apart. Both presenters gave it 4.4 out of 10, concluding it's not worthy of the hype.

title: Is this London’s best value lunch? (£16)

restaurants.name: Cinder
restaurants.notes: Reviewers praised the cedar plank salmon with vibrant, colorful presentation and silky smooth herb sauce. The Cinder burger (£16) received exceptional acclaim for its flame-grilled taste, charred exterior, perfectly seasoned meat, and soft yet substantial bun, described as one of the best value lunches in London.

title: The most disgusting food item in London 🤮

restaurants.name: Octopus Kebab Stall
restaurants.notes: Mobile food stall serving octopus kebabs and fish and chips. Both reviewers found it disgusting, with the octopus having a stale fish taste and the chips having an overwhelmingly horrible flavor resembling the smell of the sea. Described as overhyped and a waste of money.

title: Mid,expensive and small shawarma 👎🏼

restaurants.name: Schwarmama Bros
restaurants.notes: Chicken shawarma wrap for £8 was small and expensive. The bread was tough, salad fresh but sparse, and there wasn't enough chicken. The sauce was too sweet and tangy. They found it underwhelming compared to other shawarma spots in London and would not recommend returning.

title: part3 of reviewing viral food in Burrough market we try the fish and chips sandwich from Applebee's

restaurants.name: Applebee's
restaurants.notes: Fish finger baguette was disappointing - bread too thick, fish too thick, not enough sauce, and very dry. The most expensive item reviewed (£12) and the most disappointing so far.

title: breakfast at Cafe Paolo in Acton 🍳🥓🤪

restaurants.name: Cafe Paolo
restaurants.notes: Full English breakfast described as breathtaking and incredible. Sausage rated 8/10, with perfectly cooked components including eggs, bacon, black pudding, white pudding, and beans. Coffee also excellent. Overall very satisfied.

title: reviewing the Ginger pig lamb sausage roll in Borough Market 🐖🌭😉

restaurants.name: Ginger Pig
restaurants.notes: They tried the lamb sausage roll and found it incredibly spiced with herbs, melting into a fatty, meaty, spicy, salty, flaky, golden, buttery pastry. Both presenters praised it highly, with Paul suggesting he preferred it slightly to the pork version.

title: we try toad bakery Sadiq Khan's favourite bakery

restaurants.name: Toad Bakery
restaurants.notes: Sadiq Khan's favorite South London bakery. They tried the blueberry and custard Danish (rated 8 and 8.625) described as having beautiful layers and a delightful mix of sweet and tart flavors, and the everything bagel croissant (rated 8.5 and 7.8) which had outstanding pastry quality though the flavors were mixed - herby and nutty with cream cheese and French cheese, but somewhat dry. Both presenters praised the bakery's elevated pastry quality comparable to German, French and Italian standards.

title: Is this the best Banh Mi in London? 🇻🇳

restaurants.name: Baguette King
restaurants.notes: Outstanding banh mi with juicy barbecue pork, well-toasted crunchy bread, and perfect spice level. Very close second to Lào Banh Mì but bigger for £9. Highly recommended.

restaurants.name: Lào Banh Mì
restaurants.notes: Their most recommended banh mì spot and current top choice. Still slightly ahead of Baguette King, though the difference is very small.

title: Is his the best bakery in Europe? 🇩🇰
Is this the best full English breakfast in London? 🍳 £16.50 paid in full

restaurants.name: Cherries Cafe
restaurants.notes: They claimed this is the best full English breakfast in London. Praised the quality of the sausages, mushrooms, bacon, black pudding, and overall breakfast at £16.50 per person. Both presenters were enthusiastic, calling it outstanding and worth every penny.

title: London’s cheap way final boss

restaurants.name: Gymkhana
restaurants.notes: They spent £700 on a curry at Gymkhana but were looking for something more modest/cheaper.

restaurants.name: Lahor Karahi
restaurants.notes: Legendary 2.50 kebab roll with fresh naan, lamb, vegetables and sauces. Gerry called it his favourite cheap eat in London, with intense fragrant flavors and great sauces. Exceptional value for money.

title: Lilly Allen’s favourite London restaurant 👀

restaurants.name: Afghan Kitchen
restaurants.notes: Afghan restaurant with hearty, comforting dishes like lamb and potato and spinach lamb. Gerry and Paul praised the good herbal flavors, swift service, and reasonable prices, though noted it's not overly spicy or complex in flavor—solid cafe-type restaurant for healthy, peasant-style food.

title: London’s best sandwich 🥪

restaurants.name: Café Mondo
restaurants.notes: Reviewed a year after opening and found it even better. Makes pork buns and other substantial sandwiches in-house with meat roasted on-site and bread baked fresh. Praised for juicy, tender, spicy sandwiches with crispy yet fluffy bread at £6 per sandwich.

title: Did you know there is a McDonald ‘s that does a McPizza, and it’s as good as you think it is… 🍕
£10 ramen at the back of a Notting Hill supermarket 🍜

restaurants.name: Robin's Ramen
restaurants.notes: Located at the back of a supermarket. Both presenters praised the £10 ramen highly, particularly the charred pork belly, deep chicken broth, and wholemeal noodles. Gerry scored 8.2, Paul scored 8.0. Exceptional value for money.

title: Is London style pizza a thing?

restaurants.name: Conny's Pizza
restaurants.notes: Thin and crispy Neapolitan-style pizza from a top 50 Neapolitan chef. Reviewers praised the vodka pizza, pepperoni, and margarita for their excellent bake, crispy crust, well-balanced flavors, and good blend of cheese. Pizza prices between £12-16.

title: Idris Elba co-owns a restaurant… is it any good?

restaurants.name: Porte Noire
restaurants.notes: Co-owned by Idris Elba. Excellent French cuisine including snails, pork belly, veal cordon bleu, and short ribs. Described as one of the best dining experiences, with perfectly seasoned beef and tender meats that impressed both reviewers.

title: Reviewing the Dave’s Hot Chicken X Fallout collab meal

restaurants.name: Dave's Hot Chicken
restaurants.notes: Gerry tried the Fallout collaboration meal with extra hot chicken burger, mac and cheese, and chips. Praised the chicken as moist, juicy and succulent with good coating. Mac and cheese was very cheesy and creamy. Noted the spice level as manageable and wanted to try their reaper challenge.

title: Best Caribbean take away in Tottenham? 🇯🇲

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Jewish deli serving jerk chicken bagel and Caribbean mac and cheese. Described as having gorgeous herbal aroma, with well-seasoned food served by nice people who follow their page. Decent hearty food served with a smile.

title: 11 January 2026

restaurants.name: Morley's
restaurants.notes: Juicy, beautifully seasoned chicken with warm peppery heat. Wings were surprisingly good and nicely cooked, though the sauce was noted as a bit too sweet.

title: part 5 discovering lit food in Deptford Morley's

restaurants.name: Molly's
restaurants.notes: South London institution serving fried chicken and burgers. Gerry gave it 5.9/10 praising the burger's solid presentation and affordability but noting unmelted cheese and subpar bun. Paul gave it 5.5/10, finding the chicken well-cooked but uncertain about the sauce. Both agreed it's tasty and affordable, good for late night, though not fine dining.

restaurants.name: Gobsmack
restaurants.notes: Mentioned as an alternative food option nearby that Gerry would prefer to spend money at over Molly's, suggesting it's a higher quality establishment.

title: Part 4 discovering lit food in Deptford Honey's

restaurants.name: Honey's
restaurants.notes: Caribbean food truck specializing in slow-cooked curries and stews. Gerry gave it 7/10, praising the goat curry and rice & peas as 'food for the soul' with beautiful slow cooking and nice spicing. Paul also rated 7/10, finding it comforting and buttery. Both appreciated the friendly service and would return.

title: part 3 of discovering lit food in Deptford we try a Philly cheese steak

restaurants.name: Little Nans
restaurants.notes: They note that Little Nans doesn't do food, but praise the decor as perhaps the best they've seen.

restaurants.name: Harland's Philly cheese steak
restaurants.notes: Gerry rated it 3.6/10, Paul rated it 4.6/10. They heavily criticized the untoasted bread, cheap stringy meat, uncooked onions, and poor quality chili sauce. Gerry said it was 'the worst Philly cheese steak I've ever had in my life.'

title: part 2 of reviewing lit food in Deptford we try the Spice truck

restaurants.name: Spice truck
restaurants.notes: Reviewed two dishes: chicken barg (7.7/10) with nicely coated spicy deep fried chicken in curry sauce, and chicken rogan josh (8.2/10) with perfect chicken and rich sauce. Both rated highly for quality at £7 each.

title: REVIEWING The viral cookie from M&S 🍪🤪

restaurants.name: Marks and Spencers
restaurants.notes: They reviewed M&S's viral pistachio cookie. Found it edible and nice but underwhelming, questioning the hype around it. Rated between 5-7 out of 10.

title: this is our visit to Hungry Dane the best burger with ever eaten 🇩🇰🍔🤪
part 5 of reviewing viral food in Borough Market bread ahead doughnuts

restaurants.name: Bread Ahead Doughnuts
restaurants.notes: Described as 'quite frankly the best donuts in the world.' They praised the cranberry doughnut for its snapping creme brulee, silky cream, and light fried doughnut with lashings of sugar. The black currant cheesecake doughnut was also highly praised as fluffy, sweet but not too sweet, with a fulfilling taste.

title: in a series discovering London institutions we visit Jamie Oliver's favourite kebab shop

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Jamie Oliver's favourite kebab shop, described as an old-fashioned London institution. They tried chicken shawarma and lamb kebab. Good quality food, fresh ingredients, open until 1am daily. A local institution that hasn't changed since the 70s-80s.

title: Part 4 of reviewing viral food in Borough Market we try the jumbo oysters from furness 🫠🦪😉

restaurants.name: Furnace Fish Grill Oyster Bar
restaurants.notes: Jumbo oysters with fresh, flavorful taste and excellent service. Paul enjoyed the experience and gave it 8.9 out of 10, calling it 100% worth the hype with short queues and friendly staff.

title: £5 jerk shawarma wrap. reviewed!🍗🌯😗

restaurants.name: Petty Co
restaurants.notes: Jerk chicken schwarma wrap for £5. Fresh chicken and salad, friendly service. Not the most flavorful but good value and decent quality ingredients. Paul gave it 6.6, Gerry gave it 6.8.

title: part3 of reviewing viral food in Burrough market 🫡 we try the fish and chips sandwich from Applebees

restaurants.name: Applebees
restaurants.notes: Fish finger baguette (£12) was disappointing - bread too thick, fish too thick, lack of sauce, and chips made it dry. Presenters felt it could have been great with softer bread, thinner fish, and more sauce.

title: Can you get a good pizza for £5 ?! 🧐we visit rancesco's in Camberwell🍕🤪#food #pizza #londoncheapeats

restaurants.name: Francesco's
restaurants.notes: Five pound pizza spot open late (till 1-2am on weekends). Good quality base and crust for the price; salty toppings with cheap but decent ingredients. Serves its purpose well despite being 'junk pizza done well'.

title: part 2 of reviewing viral food in Borough Market. RACLETTE. 🧀🫠#food #raclette #boroughmarket

restaurants.name: Raclette stall
restaurants.notes: Ogleshield cheese scraped onto new potatoes with pepper and pickled gherkins. Creamy, wonderfully salty, with perfectly cooked potatoes. Worth the viral hype according to Gerry.

restaurants.name: Spud Bros
restaurants.notes: Mentioned in comparison to the raclette stall. Paul prefers the cheese-focused raclette over Spud Bros.

restaurants.name: Black Pig
restaurants.notes: Paul mentions he would prefer to visit this stall instead of waiting 20 minutes for raclette.

restaurants.name: Ginger Pig
restaurants.notes: Paul mentions he would prefer to visit this stall instead of waiting 20 minutes for raclette.

title: Welcome to The Big Red Pizza Tour

restaurants.name: Coach Tavern
restaurants.notes: They visited this venue as part of their big red pizza tour and tried their short pizza.

title: ATTENTION.  superb pizzeria.🍕 just opened today. here's our review #bitetwice

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: A newly opened artisan New York style pizzeria. They praised the char on the pizza, the dough quality, exceptional ingredients, perfect pepperoni distribution, and the flaky yet airy cheese. The sourdough crust pizza was £30.

title: Dough hands review 😋

restaurants.name: Dough Hands
restaurants.notes: They praised the pizza highly, describing it as 'one of the best pizzas we year got' with perfect balance of ingredients and excellent crust. Compared eating it to the Titanic scene, calling it 'the perfect hybrid pizza' that made them fall in love with pizza again.

title: London's best  🍕? Dough Hands review 🫠 #pizza #bitetwice

restaurants.name: Dough Hands
restaurants.notes: Handmade pizza with nduja, burrata, flor di latte, and San Marzano. Described as one of the best pizzas they've tasted this year with perfect crust and ingredient balance.

title: Wild Flour Pizza is a vibe ✨️🍕🎩 #pizza

restaurants.name: Wild Flour Pizza
restaurants.notes: Described as potentially the best kept secret in pizza they've visited. Praised for meticulous ingredient selection and preparation, a massive oven weighing as much as three elephants, and unique hybrid dough between bread and croissant dough.

title: Detroit-style 🍕 in Brighton 🏖 #pizza #pizzaaddict #bitetwice
Best New Haven Style 🍕 UK 🇬🇧

restaurants.name: Aonan
restaurants.notes: Vincenzo slings some of the best pie in the world.

restaurants.name: Crisp
restaurants.notes: Everybody's favorite pizzeria - believe the hype, this is real New Haven style pizza.

restaurants.name: Gracie
restaurants.notes: The pizza power couple who started the entire New Haven Revolution in the UK and take it to levels.

restaurants.name: The Groa
restaurants.notes: New Kids on the Block - their pizza bangs.

title: The Christmas 🎄sandwich 🥪 you have to try! from The Black Pig @Borough_Market  #christmas2024

restaurants.name: The Black Pig
restaurants.notes: Featured for their Christmas sandwich offering that Bite Twice recommends trying.

title: is this London's highest rates pizza? 🤔

restaurants.name: Quadrata
restaurants.notes: Sells traditional Al Taglio style pizza. The video title questions if this is London's highest rated pizza, suggesting investigation rather than outright praise.

title: we found a 🎄Christmas pudding burger 🍔

restaurants.name: Patio Pizza
restaurants.notes: Bite Twice asked Alim from Patio Pizza about his best pizza; they also found a Christmas pudding burger there.

title: Alim's best 🍕

restaurants.name: Patio Pizza
restaurants.notes: Alim's recommendation for best pizza in London. Described as having crispy, fresh bread base that doesn't taste funky, with nice char.

title: We made a Chicago deep dish 🍕
Here's our first short on shorts 💥 a fiery lava pizza by Tom from Impasto micro pizzeria 🔥

restaurants.name: Impasto micro pizzeria
restaurants.notes: They reviewed a fiery lava pizza made by Tom from this micro pizzeria.

title: Is this London's best chicken burger?

restaurants.name: Eating with Tod (Festive Feast)
restaurants.notes: They reviewed a two-Michelin-starred chicken burger collaboration with Chef Magma. The burger featured an Asian-flavored crispy chicken with champagne vinegar-marinated pickles on a potato bun, priced at £15. They praised its incredible juiciness, complexity of flavors, and crunch.

title: THe Best Soulfood in London 🇯🇲🍲

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Caribbean soul food stall in Shepherd's Bush Market. Open Fridays and Saturdays, cash only. They praised the jerk chicken, fish curry with rice and peas, plantain, vegetable stew, melon punch and ginger drink as exceptional, authentic, and delicious. Described it as 'a real gem of West London' and 'beyond ratings.'

title: Afghan kitchen 🇦🇫 when Islington institution 🤪

restaurants.name: Afghan Kitchen
restaurants.notes: Gerry and Paul praised the delicious, hearty Afghan food, particularly the chicken in yogurt and lamb dishes. They noted fast service and thought it was worth the restaurant's popularity, rating it around 8/10.

title: We review Dave's hot chicken 🍗🤪

restaurants.name: Dave's Hot Chicken
restaurants.notes: They were pleasantly surprised by the fried chicken quality. The breading was excellent and not greasy, with a unique taste compared to UK offerings. The sliders scored 7.5 and the tenders scored 8.2. Gerry gave it 7.6/10 overall, Paul gave the tenders a solid 8.2/10, finding them juicy, tender and with a pleasant level of spiciness.

title: reviewing Jay rayner's favourite sandwich shop 🥪

restaurants.name: Jerry Subs
restaurants.notes: Gerry and Paul reviewed Jay Rayner's favourite Philly cheesesteak sandwich. They praised it as a wonderful, soft, tender sandwich with juicy meat, cheese, and gravy on a soft bun. Paul gave it 8/10, noting it was very tasty but the beef could be better and it's quite expensive at £14.

title: Desserts spots of London

restaurants.name: Caravaggio
restaurants.notes: Dessert shop with freshly made ice cream and warm desserts like Belgian apple pie. They offer high-quality baklava and chocolate fondant with creamy ice cream. Great location and excellent quality, with one reviewer giving it 8/10.

title: do you know a lunch deal in London better than this? 🤨

restaurants.name: Dawat
restaurants.notes: Kebab rolls for £2.49 with fresh homemade naan, well-cooked meat, and excellent yogurt-mint sauce. Presenters were impressed by the quality and value, finding it exceptional for the price in London.

title: have you ever had a Jerk burrito? 🍗🌯

restaurants.name: <UNKNOWN>
restaurants.notes: Jerk chicken shawarma stall. Fresh chicken and salad, welcoming service. £5 for a shawarma with hot sauce, coleslaw and vegetables. Gerry rated it 9/10, Paul rated it 6.8/10 for being slightly lacking in flavor brightness but good value lunch option.

title: Eating with the Bus Drivers 🚍🍳

restaurants.name: Busman's Cafe
restaurants.notes: They had a traditional English breakfast for £7. The sausages were acceptable, the bacon was well-cooked, mushrooms were fresh (not tinned), and the tea was well-made. Not in the elite breakfast league but a good affordable option.

restaurants.name: Terry's
restaurants.notes: Mentioned as an elite breakfast destination in the Southwark area, though they did not visit or review it in this video.

title: we took our duty to review the New Jersey Mike's! 🥪😐

restaurants.name: Jersey Mike's
restaurants.notes: Presenters found the sandwich overpriced and disappointing. The bread was dry and soggy, meat was tasteless, and the experience of waiting 30-40 minutes was not worth it. They felt it was an 'improved Subway' at best but ultimately not recommended, especially if hungry with no queue elsewhere.

title: we heard about a place on aholloway road serving tiramisu out of an old cash point  🤓

restaurants.name: Tiramisu ATM (Holloway Road)
restaurants.notes: They reviewed tiramisu sold from an old ATM window. The tiramisu hadn't set properly - biscuits were crispy instead of soaked, cream was too runny, and it lacked sufficient coffee flavoring. While the flavors were okay, the execution was poor and they wouldn't return.
